title: Westward-moving sea-level signals: waves, eddies or something else
query: Sea surface height anomalies in mid-latitudes move westward, and their speed has been reported to exceed what the linear theory of long planetary (Rossby) waves predicts. Proposed explanations include the mean flow and the bottom topography, and that the signals are eddies rather than waves. Using the supplied GLORYS12 monthly sea surface height, temperature, salinity and velocity for 2011-2020 in the western Tasman Sea off south-eastern Australia (46-26 S, 147-162 E), measure the westward propagation speed as a function of latitude, compare it with the speed you compute from the stratification, and determine which explanation the data support. The fields end at 1000 m and are monthly means; show how much these two limits affect the comparison.

region.name: Tasman Sea and East Australian Current
